primitives.name: World Model Policy Evaluation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Can a learned world model serve as a *policy evaluation environment* — rolling out arbitrary policies and scoring them — with results that correlate with real-world performance?
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\hat{\\rho}(\\pi)': 'Policy value estimate (dimensionless)', '\\hat{T}': 'Learned world model (unitless)', '\\hat{R}': 'Learned reward function (dimensionless)', '\\tau': 'Trajectory (unitless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Single shared physics across tasks; VLM reward accuracy; policy action chunks align with model rollout horizon.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \(\mathcal{T}\) fails to generalize to unseen actions or environments.

layer2.mapping: The policy evaluation framework \(\hat{\rho}(\pi)\) mirrors GSI's Bayesian policy value estimation, while \(\mathcal{T}\) acts as a generative simulator for GSE's state transition graph.
layer2.telemetry: Correlation between real-world and world-model success rates (Pearson r = 0.78).

primitives.name: Multi-Task Policy Rollout
primitives.verbatim_quote: Key observation (§1): many tasks/policies, but one physical world governed by one set of laws — so a single world model can evaluate any policy on any task.
primitives.assumptions: Shared deterministic dynamics across tasks; model generalization to new tasks.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When task-specific dynamics deviate beyond model capacity.

layer2.mapping: GSE derives task-specific rollouts from a shared kernel \(\hat{T}\), enabling efficient cross-task policy comparison.

primitives.name: Diffusion Horizon Alignment
primitives.verbatim_quote: (2) **Rollout:** policy outputs action chunk a_pred; world model denoises |a_pred| frames in parallel — diffusion horizon flexibly matched to the policy's chunk size (vs Cosmos's fixed 16-frame bidirectional context, which wastes compute).
primitives.assumptions: Policy action chunks are aligned with model diffusion steps; no computational waste due to fixed horizons.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When policy chunk size exceeds model’s effective horizon.

layer2.mapping: GSE aligns its simulation horizon with policy decision cadence, mirroring the diffusion alignment principle in GSI's temporal consistency checks.
layer2.telemetry: Compute time reduced to <1 hour vs days of real-world eval.
